title: Test the pt2 pickle guard by rewriting the archive's sample-inputs record with a marker payload
answers: how to test pt2 pickle payload rejection
write a test for malicious pt2 archive with MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION false
simulate a pickle payload inside a pt2 model archive
body:
Use _replace_pt2_sample_inputs_record in tests/pytorch/test_pytorch_model_export.py: it torch.save()s an object whose __reduce__ creates a marker file, then rewrites the zip entry in data/model.pt2. It matches both the legacy serialized_example_inputs.pt name and the /sample_inputs/ path, so it works across torch versions.
Assert both mlflow.pytorch.load_model and mlflow.pyfunc.load_model raise MlflowException with match=f"record '{re.escape(record)}'", and that the marker file does not exist afterwards.
Positive-path and marker tests need the @pytest.mark.skipif(Version(torch.__version__) < Version("2.10")) gate; monkeypatch MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION to "false" with monkeypatch.setenv.
For the version-refusal path, use mock.patch("torch.__version__", "2.9.1") rather than installing another torch.
applies: Unit tests for the pytorch pt2 load path in tests/pytorch.
says: Loading an untrusted PyTorch model executes arbitrary code instead of being blocked.
The model serving endpoint fails to reject model packages containing unsafe serialized payloads.
Prevent execution of unauthorized serialization code when opening downloaded model archives.
Model deployment raises no security error when reading suspicious sample input records.
search: Testing the PyTorch pt2 pickle guard involves replacing zip entries in data/model.pt2 using _replace_pt2_sample_inputs_record with an object whose __reduce__ creates a marker file. In tests/pytorch/test_pytorch_model_export.py, both mlflow.pytorch.load_model and mlflow.pyfunc.load_model must raise MlflowException with the matching record name, ensuring the marker file is not created. Tests require monkeypatching MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION to 'false', gating on torch version 2.10 or higher, and mocking torch.__version__ as '2.9.1' for version refusal.
